name: South India (Tamil Nadu · Kerala · Karnataka · Telangana)

language.script: Dravidian scripts — Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam (each visually distinct)
language.script_notes: Four distinct Dravidian scripts, each rounded and visually different both from Devanagari and from each other once you learn their basic letterforms — a strong, reliable regional tell.
false_friends: Sri Lanka (shares Tamil script/language in the north of the island)
North India (same country, very different script/architecture)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: More consistent maintenance in tech-hub cities (Bengaluru, Hyderabad).

architecture.roof_style: The towering, intricately carved gopuram gateway tower is the defining South Indian Dravidian temple signature, visible from a distance.
architecture.roof_material: Traditional sloped clay-tile roofs more common in Kerala given higher rainfall.
architecture.wall_construction: Dravidian-style temple complexes with multiple concentric walled courtyards and soaring carved gopurams; colonial-era architecture along the coast (Kochi, Chennai); modern tech-park glass architecture in Bengaluru/Hyderabad.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Brightly painted, intricately carved gopuram towers (often multicoloured) are the strongest single visual tell; whitewashed or red-tile Keralan houses.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Dravidian temple complexes with towering carved gopurams; Kerala's backwater houseboats and sloped-roof houses; colonial Portuguese/Dutch/British-era coastal architecture; modern IT-park development in Bengaluru/Hyderabad.

nature.vegetation: Dense, biodiverse tropical evergreen rainforest along the Western Ghats (among the wettest regions in India); coconut palm groves and backwaters along the Kerala coast; drier scrub on the Deccan Plateau interior (Karnataka/Telangana).
nature.terrain: The Western Ghats mountain range runs along the west coast, with a narrow, lush coastal plain (Kerala/coastal Karnataka) below it; the Deccan Plateau covers the interior; the Eastern Ghats and Bay of Bengal coastline lie to the east (Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh).
nature.climate_signature: Noticeably greener and more consistently humid than North India, especially near the Western Ghats and Kerala coast; strong monsoon influence.

vehicles.plate_color: Tamil Nadu ('TN'), Karnataka ('KA'), Kerala ('KL'), Telangana ('TS') state codes.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavier IT-sector commuter traffic in Bengaluru/Hyderabad.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Better official Google coverage in tech-hub cities (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai) than much of the north.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Generally denser and more consistently modern coverage than rural North India, reflecting the region's tech-sector development.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Tamil language/script presence, similar tropical coastal palm vegetation and Dravidian-influenced temple architecture in Sri Lanka's north
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Sri Lanka is an island using Sinhala script predominantly (with Tamil in the north/east only); South Indian coverage is denser and includes the mainland's clearly continental road network and Indian plate formats.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same general road furniture and flat-concrete-roof default
confusion_set.tiebreaker: South India uses Dravidian scripts with towering carved gopuram temple gateways; North India uses Devanagari/Gurmukhi script with curved Nagara-style shikhara towers instead — an unmistakable difference once either is visible.
